title: Bandwidth-Conscious Mobile SDK: Fidelity Pacing & Resumable Tool Transactions (PRD draft)
summary: Draft PRD proposing a lightweight, energy- and bandwidth-aware mobile SDK for Redwood's Hosted API. Focus is on adaptive fidelity pacing for streaming outputs, delta-compressed typed frames for structured output, and resumable microtransactions for tool calls to support intermittent connectivity and low-power devices.
goals: Reduce perceived user latency on metered mobile networks by adapting fidelity rather than blocking for high-quality outputs
Limit network energy use for mobile clients via an SDK pacing governor and optional energy-budget header negotiation
Ensure tool-calls (e.g., external API invocations, DB writes) are resumable and idempotent across connectivity interruptions
Provide a compact typed-frame format and delta compression to reduce bytes for structured outputs and partial updates
Offer simple SDK ergonomics for quick adoption: 3 APIs (stream, call, checkpoint) with clear defaults for mobile constraints
non_goals: Reinventing end-to-end offline storage (we will integrate with platform-level offline caches rather than replace them)
Guaranteeing identical model output across fidelity modes—some variance is acceptable when trading quality for bytes/energy
Full parity with desktop SDK feature set on first rollout
assumptions: Primary early users are mobile-first apps with metered data (messaging, note-taking, on-device assistants)
Hosted API can expose lightweight negotiation headers and a compact binary/JSON-Lite frame format without breaking existing clients
We can add telemetry hooks for energy and bytes without unacceptable privacy or perf costs
Model variants with graceful-quality-reduction modes are available (e.g., short-token heuristics, lower-temperature samplers, quantized candidates)
metrics: Avg bytes per streamed session (target: -30% vs baseline)
Rate of successful resumable tool-call commits after reconnect (target: >99%)
Energy proxy metric: client-side active-radio-time per session (requires mobile SDK telemetry)
Adoption: number of mobile apps using fidelity pacing APIs within 6 months
user_personas: Mobile app engineer: needs small bytes, predictable UX, minimal extra server work
Platform/SDK integrator: wants ergonomic APIs and safe defaults for flaky networks
Product PM: cares about engagement on low-data users and predictable cost per session
product_requirements: 1) Fidelity Pacing API: SDK exposes a single optional 'fidelityBudget' param (bytes or energy proxy) and a streaming mode 'pacing: {aggressive|balanced|conservative}'. Server returns progressive frames sized to stay within budget.
2) Typed Delta Frames: structured output uses compact frames that encode only changed fields (delta) plus minimal schema id. Support JSON-Lite (text) and CBOR-lite (binary) encodings.

3) Microburst Coalescer: client-side coalescing of rapid user edits into a single upstream event to avoid multiple short tokens causing inefficient server batching. Configurable debounce window default 150ms.

4) Resumable Tool Transactions: tool-calls are split into 'prepare' (idempotent, returns a transaction token) and 'commit' phases. SDK persists tokens to storage and retries commit on reconnect. Server exposes idempotency surface with TTL for tokens.

5) Pacing Governor: SDK monitors network RTT and radio state (where available) to slow down fidelity when the energy proxy exceeds thresholds. Provides programmatic callbacks for app UX (onQualityDownshift, onQualityRestore).
6) Fallback Variants: when budget exhausted, server returns a compact summary variant plus an optional 'continue' token allowing the client to fetch higher-fidelity deltas when on better network.

7) Telemetry and Privacy: collect bytes, session-mode, fidelity-changes, transaction success/failure. Only collect device-level energy proxies as aggregated counters; do not collect raw battery history or PII.
8) SDK Ergonomics: three surface methods: streamGenerate(request, opts), toolCall(callSpec, opts), checkpoint(stateKey). Default opts keep developer effort minimal; advanced knobs for platform teams.
9) Backwards Compatibility: server must honor requests without fidelity headers for legacy clients; new features opt-in by presence of headers or SDK version.
sdk_api_sketch: checkpoint(key) => persists SDK state (pending transactions, sessionHandle) to platform local storage for resume after kill/restart
streaming_behavior: Server sends 'initial-frame' (compact summary) quickly, sized small to start the UX
Subsequent frames are delta-encoded and labeled with sequence numbers and schema ids
Frames include optional 'qualityHint' (numeric) so client UI can render gracefully (e.g., skeleton -> draft -> final)
If server detects client-specified budget exceeded, attach 'budget_exhausted' flag and a 'continue_token' for fetch-later semantics
Client applies microburst coalescing: short bursts of input are merged client-side to reduce request count and upstream tokenization cost
tool_call_contracts: Prepare/Commit split: prepare returns transactionToken and an optimistic preview of changes; commit finalizes and emits server-side effects
Idempotency: token can be submitted repeatedly; server ensures single commit with token TTL (default 24h) and opaque transaction status endpoint
Partial-results: tools may return provisional outputs streamed back before commit (useful for long-running external ops)

Conflict semantics: if commit sees a conflicting state, server returns conflict resolution hints and a retriable error code; SDK surfaces to app for user-level merge or automatic resolution when policy allows
resume_and_offline: SDK persists minimal resume state: sessionHandle, latestSequence, outstanding transactionTokens
On reconnect, SDK replays commit operations using transaction tokens and fetches missing frames using latestSequence/continue_token
Offline UX: SDK can synthesize a cached summary from last known final frame; apps can opt-in to allow local edits that are queued as microbursts
Storage: small on-device key-value (max few KBs per session); respect platform storage best-practices and expose clear eviction signal to app
Security: transactionTokens are scoped to account/app; persisted tokens are encrypted by platform storage where available
telemetry_and_observability: Client-side metrics: bytes_sent, bytes_recv, session_radio_time_ms (proxy), fidelity_changes_count, transactions_committed, transactions_retried
Server-side metrics: average frame size by pacing mode, commit-latency, resume-success-rate
Tracing: associate sessionHandle with server traces for p50/p95 latency investigations (opt-in at app-level)
Alerting: resume-success-rate drop below threshold should alert infra and product for potential protocol/regression issues
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (experiment): internal dogfood SDK with 2 apps, opt-in telemetry, validate bytes and resume success
Phase 1 (beta): limited external partners; gated by SDK version and feature flags; collect UX feedback for pacing defaults
Phase 2 (public): default for mobile SDKs if experiment thresholds met; document migration and opt-out guidance
Phase 3 (stabilize): expand schema registry, add binary CBOR-lite support, tune model variant selection for graceful degrade
open_questions: Q1: What server-side budget enforcement granularity is practical (per-frame vs per-session)?
Q2: Do we expose a standard energy proxy header (e.g., X-REDWOOD-ENERGY-BUDGET) or keep it internal to SDK negotiation?
Q3: How long should transactionTokens live? Default 24h may be too long for some use-cases; need policy for cleanup and replay cost
Q4: Will delta-encoding interact poorly with existing schema-evolution? Need a small schema registry and version compatibility rules
Q5: What privacy constraints do legal/security teams require for energy/telemetry signals from clients?
appendix: - Client request headers: X-REDWOOD-SDK-V:2, X-REDWOOD-FIDELITY-BYTES:10240, X-REDWOOD-PACING:balanced
- Server response frames: {seq:1, schema:22, delta: '...base64 or json-lite...', qualityHint:0.6, continueToken:?}
Appendix B: Example flow (chat with a background tool call):
2) server sends initial-frame (short summary), client renders immediately
3) server starts prepare for a tool call (db write) -> returns transactionToken streamed
4) client shows provisional result while offline; when online, SDK calls commit(transactionToken) -> server responds commit_ok
Appendix C: UX guidance for partners: expose low/medium/high quality toggle mapped to pacing modes; always show 'loading fidelity' indicator when quality downshifted
